content.text:
## The programmes

*(Caveat up front: my literature searching hit a quota partway through, so claims dated 2026 are from background knowledge rather than freshly verified. I flag the weakest-verified points below.)*

---

### 1. Cold, collisionless dark matter as a cosmological framework (ΛCDM)

This is the substrate claim — that ~5/6 of the matter density is non-relativistic, non-baryonic and effectively pressureless — rather than a claim about a specific particle. It rests on quantitatively independent lines: CMB acoustic peak morphology (Planck Collaboration, *Planck 2018 results VI: cosmological parameters*, A&A 2020, giving Ω_c h² ≈ 0.12), baryon acoustic oscillations in galaxy surveys (SDSS/eBOSS; DESI DR1–DR2 papers, 2024–2025), weak-lensing shear (DES, KiDS, HSC), cluster mass budgets, and the Lyman-α forest. The dark-baryon distinction is doubly pinned by Big Bang nucleosynthesis and the CMB agreeing on the baryon density. Collisionless behaviour is directly evidenced by the lensing/gas offset in merging clusters (Clowe et al., "A Direct Empirical Proof of the Existence of Dark Matter", ApJL 2006). Crucially it made pre-registered predictions later confirmed: the BAO scale and amplitude, the relative heights of the CMB peaks, and the existence of large populations of ultra-faint satellites subsequently found by SDSS/DES/Pan-STARRS. Open irritants are astrophysical, not foundational: the tightness of the radial-acceleration relation (McGaugh, Lelli & Schombert, PRL 2016), residual core–cusp and satellite-plane puzzles, and the σ₈/S₈ tension — all currently absorbed into baryonic-feedback modelling, which is where the post-hoc risk sits.

**Verdict: solid**
**Principal problem (if fragile or worse):** none

---

### 2. WIMPs / weak-scale thermal relics

The best-instrumented programme and the one with the clearest null result. Three multi-tonne xenon time-projection chambers now run on three continents — LZ at SURF (US), XENONnT at Gran Sasso (Italy), PandaX-4T at Jinping (China) — plus argon detectors DarkSide-50 and DEAP-3600 (see the review *Dark matter direct detection: status, results and future plans*, arXiv:2512.23039, 2025). LZ's 4.2 tonne-year exposure (LUX-ZEPLIN Collaboration, PRL 2025; 280 live days) found no excess, pushing spin-independent limits to roughly 2×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² near 40 GeV — within about an order of magnitude of the irreducible neutrino background (the "neutrino fog", per C. O'Hare, PRL 2021). Collider searches (ATLAS/CMS missing-energy and SUSY programmes, 2015–2025) have removed most natural weak-scale supersymmetric parameter space; indirect signals are ambiguous, with the Fermi-LAT Galactic-centre excess broadly favoured to be unresolved millisecond pulsars. The one persistent positive claim, DAMA/LIBRA's annual modulation, has not been reproduced by NaI replicas ANAIS-112 (Spain) and COSINE-100 (Korea), and XENON1T's 2020 electron-recoil excess vanished in XENONnT. The programme is healthy institutionally (XLZD consortium for a ~60–80 t successor) but its original motivation — the "WIMP miracle" tied to electroweak-scale new physics — has been eroded, and the target has been serially relaxed rather than confirmed.

**Verdict: inconclusive-by-evidence**
**Principal problem (if fragile or worse):** motivating theory eroded; goalposts repeatedly moved

---

### 3. QCD axion and axion-like particles

The strongest *theoretical* case, because the axion is a by-product of a separate unsolved problem — the strong-CP problem (Peccei & Quinn, PRL 1977; Weinberg and Wilczek, PRL 1978) — with a known cosmological production route (misalignment: Preskill, Wise & Wilczek; Abbott & Sikivie; Dine & Fischler, all Phys. Lett. B 1983). Experimentally it is the fastest-growing and most geographically distributed effort: ADMX at Washington has now scanned 1.1–1.3 GHz (~4.5–5.4 µeV) at DFSZ sensitivity (ADMX Collaboration, PRL 135, 191001, 2025); CAPP-MAX at IBS/KAIST in Korea has extended searches above 1 GHz (Phys. Rev. X 14, 031023, 2024); HAYSTAC (Yale), ORGAN (Western Australia), QUAX (Italy), MADMAX (Germany), DMRadio and ABRACADABRA/SHAFT (US), CASPEr (Mainz/Boston) and BabyIAXO cover complementary mass decades. Lattice-informed simulations of axion-string networks predict a post-inflationary mass in the tens-of-µeV range (e.g. Buschmann et al., Nature Communications 2022), giving the programme a genuine falsifiable target. Against it: no detection, and the allowed mass spans many decades, so null results exclude only slivers — the programme's testability is real but slow.

**Verdict: defensible with reservations**
**Principal problem (if fragile or worse):** none (but parameter space is vast)

---

### 4. Dark sectors: sub-GeV light dark matter and self-interacting dark matter

A single family with two faces. Astrophysically, self-interacting dark matter is now treated as a mature phenomenology: the recent review *Astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions* (Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004, 2025) argues that light-mediator or strongly-coupled dark sectors arise generically and that SIDM plausibly explains the observed *diversity* of galactic rotation curves — including both unusually dense and unusually cored dwarfs via gravothermal core collapse. Experimentally, the MeV–GeV frontier is expanding fast: skipper-CCD and cryogenic detectors (SENSEI, DAMIC-M, SuperCDMS), and accelerator probes of dark photons and light mediators (NA64 at CERN, Belle II at KEK, LDMX in preparation). The reservation is flexibility: the self-interaction cross-section's velocity dependence has substantial freedom, and much SIDM fitting is retrodictive. The clearest earned credit is that SIDM predicted a *scatter*-based signature (dense, collapsed haloes alongside cored ones) before the observations of anomalously dense subhaloes in lensing systems.

**Verdict: defensible with reservations**
**Principal problem (if fragile or worse):** none (watch parameter freedom)

---

### 5. Primordial black holes and macroscopic dark matter

Attractive because it needs no new particle, only non-vanilla inflationary physics to seed the required density perturbation. The constraint landscape is now nearly closed: stellar microlensing toward the Magellanic Clouds and M31 (EROS, OGLE, MACHO, Subaru-HSC) plus CMB accretion, dynamical and evaporation limits leave essentially only the "asteroid-mass" window ~10¹⁷–10²³ g. Recent work stresses that even these limits depend on halo density and velocity-distribution assumptions (A. M. Green, *Primordial black hole stellar microlensing constraints*, JCAP 04 (2025) 023), i.e. the corner is soft-edged rather than airtight; see also Carr, Kohri, Sendouda & Yokoyama, Rep. Prog. Phys. 2021, and Green & Kavanagh, J. Phys. G 2021. LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA black-hole mergers gave the programme a burst of activity after 2016, but the population is better explained astrophysically and cannot supply all the dark matter. Many groups, many instruments — but the surviving window has no distinctive positive signal.

**Verdict: fragile**
**Principal problem (if fragile or worse):** viable mass window squeezed to a narrow corner with no positive signal

---

### 6. Ultralight / wave ("fuzzy") dark matter

Motivated by string-axiverse expectations and by the promise of solving small-scale structure problems through a de Broglie wavelength of kiloparsec scale (Hu, Barkana & Gruzinov, PRL 2000; review by Hui, Ostriker, Tremaine & Witten, PRD 2017). The canonical ~10⁻²² eV band that would produce dwarf-galaxy cores is now in serious trouble: Lyman-α forest limits (Iršič et al., PRL 2017) and especially stellar-kinematic heating limits in ultra-faint dwarfs (Dalal & Kravtsov, JCAP 2022) push the mass many orders of magnitude higher, at which point the motivating astrophysical payoff disappears and the candidate becomes observationally indistinguishable from cold dark matter. Pulsar-timing and atomic-clock/interferometer searches (NANOGrav, optical-clock comparisons) add complementary bounds but no signals. The programme is theoretically active and internationally spread, yet its distinctive predictions were tested and largely failed.

**Verdict: fragile**
**Principal problem (if fragile or worse):** the motivating mass range is excluded

---

### 7. keV sterile neutrinos / warm dark matter

Once the most attractive "minimal" extension — the νMSM (Asaka & Shaposhnikov, Phys. Lett. B 2005) linked dark matter to neutrino masses and the baryon asymmetry with three right-handed neutrinos. Its empirical anchor was the 3.5 keV X-ray line reported in clusters and M31 (Bulbul et al., ApJ 2014; Boyarsky et al., PRL 2014), which motivated a decade of modelling — e.g. Rudakovskyi & Iakubovskyi, MNRAS 483, 4080 (2019), who argued reionisation data mildly favour a 7 keV sterile neutrino over pure CDM, while themselves noting the line's status was under debate. That debate has effectively resolved against the signal: blank-sky XMM-Newton analyses (Dessert, Rodd & Safdi, Science 2020) and NuSTAR searches find no line at the required strength. Meanwhile Lyman-α forest and Milky Way satellite counts exclude the warm free-streaming lengths that made the model interesting. Activity has thinned to a few directions (KATRIN/TRISTAN laboratory searches, XRISM microcalorimeter follow-up). I am least confident about 2025–2026 XRISM results here.

**Verdict: fragile**
**Principal problem (if fragile or worse):** flagship signal refuted; structure limits close the window

---

### 8. Modified gravity without dark matter (MOND and relativistic descendants)

The one genuinely rival framework, and the one with the best record of *advance* prediction on its home turf: Milgrom's 1983 ApJ papers predicted flat rotation curves' amplitude from baryons alone, yielding the baryonic Tully–Fisher relation and low-surface-brightness rotation-curve shapes, later codified as the radial acceleration relation (McGaugh, Lelli & Schombert, PRL 2016). ΛCDM must explain that regularity through feedback; MOND gets it for free. Beyond galaxies it fails: clusters still require unseen mass in MOND, merging-cluster lensing offsets are naturally collisionless-matter phenomena, and no relativistic completion reproduces the CMB and matter power spectrum without effectively reintroducing a dark component — TeVeS (Bekenstein, PRD 2004) was damaged by the GW170817 photon/graviton speed constraint, and AeST (Skordis & Złośnik, PRL 2021) is a live but heavily engineered attempt. The current decisive test, wide binaries in Gaia, is genuinely contested: Chae (ApJ 2023–2024) reports MOND-like acceleration excesses, while analyses modelling hidden triple contamination find Newtonian behaviour and exclude MOND at high confidence (e.g. *Wide Binaries from Gaia DR3: testing GR vs MOND with realistic triple modelling*, arXiv:2504.07569, 2025, updating a 2023 study). The community is small and the disputes are largely between a handful of groups.

**Verdict: fragile**
**Principal problem (if fragile or worse):** cluster and cosmological failures; no viable relativistic completion

---

## Ranking, best to worst current shape

1. **ΛCDM cold collisionless framework** — the only one with multiple mutually independent measurement classes, confirmed advance predictions, and instrumentation spread across dozens of collaborations and countries. Its weaknesses are parameter-level, not existence-level.
2. **QCD axion** — no signal, but the motivation is external to dark matter and undiminished, the theory is tightly constrained, and the programme is expanding across at least eight countries with a concrete predicted mass band.
3. **Dark sectors / SIDM** — actively producing astrophysical and accelerator results, coheres with standard field theory, and has begun making distinctive predictions; discounted for parameter freedom.
4. **WIMPs** — extraordinary experimental quality and independence, but a decade of increasingly stringent nulls and a degraded theoretical rationale. Ranked below the axion because its motivation, not just its parameter space, has been undermined.
5. **Primordial black holes** — economical and instrumented by gravitational-wave and lensing surveys, but reduced to one narrow surviving mass window.
6. **Fuzzy / ultralight dark matter** — tested where it mattered and largely excluded there.
7. **keV sterile neutrinos** — flagship signal refuted; the programme has gone quiet relative to its 2014–2018 peak.
8. **MOND / modified gravity** — genuine galaxy-scale predictive successes, but framework-level failure at cluster and cosmological scales, dependence on ad hoc relativistic completions, and a concentrated, contested community.

**Where I am unsure:** the WIMP-vs-axion ordering is close and could flip on how much weight one gives "informativeness of nulls" (WIMP nulls are far more informative) versus "durability of motivation" (axion wins). Placing MOND last rather than seventh is also a judgement call: sterile-neutrino dark matter is a dead-ish candidate, whereas MOND is a live framework that is simply wrong about clusters — one could argue a wrong-but-productive framework is in better shape than a refuted candidate. And I could not verify 2026 outputs (XLZD milestones, XRISM line searches, new Gaia wide-binary analyses).

**Strongest:** ΛCDM cold collisionless dark matter as a framework — the evidence is multi-instrument, multi-national, cross-checked, and includes predictions made before the data.
**Weakest:** MOND-type modified gravity — succeeds locally, fails globally, and cannot yet be written down relativistically without smuggling in what it denies.
**Worth checking further:** the Gaia wide-binary test (the cleanest MOND falsification test available, currently deadlocked over triple-star contamination); the tens-of-µeV axion band that string-network simulations single out; whether anomalously dense lensing subhaloes really require self-interactions; and XRISM's high-resolution verdict on any narrow keV X-ray lines.
**Best objection to this verdict:** that I have rewarded institutional scale and funding momentum and called it evidential health. On a strict "confirmed novel predictions per unit effort" metric, MOND outperforms the WIMP programme — MOND predicted rotation-curve shapes that were then found, while WIMP searches have produced only exclusions after several billion dollars. If that metric dominated, MOND would rise several places and WIMPs would fall. I resist this because a theory that fails on clusters, the CMB and structure formation is failing on the *majority* of the evidence, and breadth of successful domain coverage should outweigh elegance within one domain — but the objection is not frivolous, and it is the main reason I label MOND "fragile" rather than refuted.
